summary: Georgios T. Halkias works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA and MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble, later becoming Endowed Professor at the University of Hong Kong in 2025.

Gerald B. Kelley worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1952–1955), where he served as an assistant professor (~1959–1963), before becoming a professor at Cornell University in 1963.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (~1969–1974). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989) and subsequently at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (~1994–2015).

Gerald James Larson specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He was a religious studies professor at UC Santa Barbara from 1972 and Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University Bloomington in 1995.

Gerald Patrick Moriarty was an Indology and history scholar. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (BA 1881–1885), served as an Oxford tutor (~1889–1914), and was University Teacher of Indian History at the University of Cambridge (1897–1924).

Gerald Schwedler is a historian who studied at Heidelberg University (1994–2002). He served as a substitute professor at Konstanz and Heidelberg, a research assistant at the University of Zurich (2015–2018), and joined Kiel University in 2018.

Gerard Abraham Joseph was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a member of the Ceylon Civil Service and was appointed Secretary and Librarian at the National Museum of Colombo in 1893.

Gerard Leslie Makins Clauson was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1910–1914), and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Gerardus van der Leeuw worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University (~1908–1916) and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 until 1950.

Gerasim Stepanovich Lebedev was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Das in 1787. He served as an interpreter for the Collegium of Foreign Affairs in 1801 and worked at the Département asiatique (~1802–1817).
Gerd J. R. Mevissen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who held posts at the Free University of Berlin, attested in 2017 and as Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter in 2026.
Gerda Hartmann was an Indologist who earned her PhD at Kiel University under Friedrich Otto Schrader (~1928–1932). She later held a post at the Library of Congress from 1938 to 1940.

Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University (~1991–1996) and under Yasuo Yuasa, later holding academic posts at Luther College (~2000) and the University of Hong Kong (~2008–2009).

Gergana Ruseva earned an MA in Indology from Sofia University (1995–2005). She worked as a physicist at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences (2000–2009) and was a lecturer (2000) and associate professor (2012) at Sofia University.

Gergely Hidas is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He was a Khyentse Fellow at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and a postdoctoral researcher at the British Museum in 2014.

Gergely Orosz is a Tibetology scholar who worked as a librarian at the Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (attested 2002). He earned a PhD from Budapest University of Technology and Economics, becoming an assistant professor there in 2023.

Gerhard Czerny was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under Julius von Negelein and Paul Althaus, attending the universities of Vienna (1923–1925), Rostock (1925), and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1925–1927).

Gerhard Meiser was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies across several institutions, including the universities of Regensburg (~1972–1973), Munich (~1973–1977), Sarajevo, Belgrade, and Freiburg (~1977–1979).

Gerhard Oberhammer worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning a PhD at Innsbruck (~1948–1954) and studying under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. After working at Utrecht University, he served as professor at the University of Vienna (1964–1997).

Gerhard Wolf is a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Heidelberg University (~1973–1989). He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1995–1998), Trier University (~1998–2003), and the Max Planck Society (~2003).
